A.explanation: Friction is caused by contact and interlocking between surfaces, not by a fluid pressure difference.

B.explanation: Upthrust is the net upward force from higher pressure at greater depth acting on a submerged body.

C.explanation: Viscous force is caused by relative motion and shearing between fluid layers, not just static pressure difference.

D.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force on a mass, $W = mg$, and does not require any pressure difference.

hints: Notice the key wording `only by a pressure difference` - which force would still exist with no contact, no motion and no gravity from fluid alone?
Recall that fluid pressure increases with depth as $p = h\rho g$, so the bottom of a submerged object feels greater pressure than the top.
Compare the origins: friction needs surfaces rubbing, viscous force needs flow past an object, and weight needs a gravitational field.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: find the force whose sole cause is that pressure acts differently on different parts of an object.
Recall the pressure rule in a fluid: pressure increases with depth, $p = h\rho g$, so upward pressure on the lower surface exceeds downward pressure on the upper surface.
The net result is an upward force equal to the weight of displaced fluid, $F = \rho V g$, called upthrust or Archimedes force.
Check the others: friction needs normal contact, viscous force needs relative motion through a fluid, and weight needs mass in a gravitational field.
Only upthrust fits the description of being caused only by a pressure difference. This is option B
